gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of full sun each kit's own panel needs to refill its battery, or what each kit costs per Wh. Worked out from maker specs and today's maker-store prices: Elite 30 V2 + 100 W takes 2.9 h at $1.70/Wh, DELTA 3 Classic + 220 W takes 4.7 h at $0.65/Wh, AC180 + 200 W takes 5.8 h at $0.67/Wh, and AC180 + 100 W takes 11.5 h (about 3 days at 4 peak-sun hours) at $0.59/Wh.
standout_why: Compared against three pages. powerstationgearlab.com (cited) names no panel wattage and gives only wall-charge times. flowersofvice.com (cited) has one figure close to this: Jackery's own 7.5 h estimate for the 1000 v2 with one 200 W panel. It also has a general 800 Wh/day example for a 200 W panel, but no per-kit refill hours and no cost per Wh. wattfolk.com reviews panels only, with no batteries, and works out yearly kWh and payback, not refill time. urbangridbackup.com (cited) would not open (TLS certificate error), so I can't rule out that it has this. ChatGPT's own answer gives a daily kWh per panel size but never relates it to any kit's battery.
decides: It supports the DELTA 3 Classic + 220 W as the pick: it is the cheapest of the kits that refill in under 5 rated-sun hours, at $0.65/Wh and $669 on EcoFlow's US store today, which is less than the $729 Best Buy card ChatGPT showed. It also shows that the AC180 + 100 W kit on our current page needs about 3 sunny balcony days to refill. So we should list AC180 + 200 W ($769, 5.8 h) instead. The Elite 30 V2 + 100 W refills fastest (2.9 h) but costs about 2.6× more per Wh, so it is the small-battery pick for daily top-ups, not for outage backup.
